audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Hellenists/Hebrews complaint, seven appointed, Stephen, synagogue dispute, false witnesses.

verses.restored: In these days, as the disciples were multiplying, a murmuring arose of the Hellenists against the Hebrews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily service.

familiar.text: And in those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplied, there arose a murmuring of the Grecians against the Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration.

modern.text: In those days when the disciples were increasing in number, the Grecian Jews among them began to grumble against the Hebraic Jews because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food.

original.text: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις πληθυνόντων τῶν μαθητῶν ἐγένετο γογγυσμὸς τῶν Ἑλληνιστῶν πρὸς τοὺς Ἑβραίους ὅτι παρεθεωροῦντο ἐν τῇ διακονίᾳ τῇ καθημερινῇ αἱ χῆραι αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: The twelve called the multitude of the disciples and said, It is not pleasing for us to leave the word of the Divine to serve tables.

familiar.text: Then the twelve called the multitude of the disciples unto them, and said, It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables.

modern.text: So the Twelve summoned all the disciples and said, “It is unacceptable for us to neglect the word of God in order to wait on tables.

original.text: προσκαλεσάμενοι δὲ οἱ δώδεκα τὸ πλῆθος τῶν μαθητῶν εἶπαν· Οὐκ ἀρεστόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς καταλείψαντας τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ διακονεῖν τραπέζαις·

verses.restored: Therefore, siblings, look for seven men from among you, witnessed as full of Spirit and wisdom, whom we will appoint over this need.

familiar.text: Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.

modern.text: Therefore, brothers, select from among you seven men confirmed to be full of the Spirit and wisdom. We will appoint this responsibility to them

original.text: ἐπισκέψασθε ⸀δέ, ἀδελφοί, ἄνδρας ἐξ ὑμῶν μαρτυρουμένους ἑπτὰ πλήρεις ⸀πνεύματος καὶ σοφίας, οὓς ⸀καταστήσομεν ἐπὶ τῆς χρείας ταύτης·

verses.restored: But we will persevere in prayer and in the service of the word.

familiar.text: But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word.

modern.text: and will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word.”

original.text: ἡμεῖς δὲ τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ τῇ διακονίᾳ τοῦ λόγου προσκαρτερήσομεν.

verses.restored: The word pleased the whole multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of trust and holy Spirit, and Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte from Antioch.

familiar.text: And the saying pleased the whole multitude: and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch:

modern.text: This proposal pleased the whole group. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, as well as Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas from Antioch, a convert to Judaism.

original.text: καὶ ἤρεσεν ὁ λόγος ἐνώπιον παντὸς τοῦ πλήθους, καὶ ἐξελέξαντο Στέφανον, ἄνδρα ⸀πλήρης πίστεως καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου, καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Πρόχορον καὶ Νικάνορα καὶ Τίμωνα καὶ Παρμενᾶν καὶ Νικόλαον προσήλυτον Ἀντιοχέα,

verses.restored: These they set before the apostles, and praying, they laid hands on them.

familiar.text: Whom they set before the apostles: and when they had prayed, they laid their hands on them.

modern.text: They presented these seven to the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.

original.text: οὓς ἔστησαν ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀποστόλων, καὶ προσευξάμενοι ἐπέθηκαν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας.

verses.restored: The word of the Divine kept growing, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem multiplied greatly; even a great crowd of the priests were obeying the trust.

familiar.text: And the word of God increased; and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly; and a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.

modern.text: So the word of God continued to spread. The number of disciples in Jerusalem grew rapidly, and a great number of priests became obedient to the faith. The Arrest of Stephen

original.text: Καὶ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ηὔξανεν, καὶ ἐπληθύνετο ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν μαθητῶν ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ σφόδρα, πολύς τε ὄχλος τῶν ἱερέων ὑπήκουον τῇ πίστει.

verses.restored: Stephen, full of grace and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people.

familiar.text: And Stephen, full of faith and power, did great wonders and miracles among the people.

modern.text: Now Stephen, who was full of grace and power, was performing great wonders and signs among the people.

original.text: Στέφανος δὲ πλήρης ⸀χάριτος καὶ δυνάμεως ἐποίει τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα μεγάλα ἐν τῷ λαῷ.

verses.restored: But some from the synagogue called Freedmen, and Cyrenians, Alexandrians, and those from Cilicia and Asia, rose and disputed with Stephen.

familiar.text: Then there arose certain of the synagogue, which is called the synagogue of the Libertines, and Cyrenians, and Alexandrians, and of them of Cilicia and of Asia, disputing with Stephen.

modern.text: But resistance arose from what was called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, including Cyrenians, Alexandrians, and men from the provinces of Cilicia and Asia. They began to argue with Stephen,

original.text: ἀνέστησαν δέ τινες τῶν ἐκ τῆς συναγωγῆς τῆς λεγομένης Λιβερτίνων καὶ Κυρηναίων καὶ Ἀλεξανδρέων καὶ τῶν ἀπὸ Κιλικίας καὶ Ἀσίας συζητοῦντες τῷ Στεφάνῳ,

verses.restored: They were not able to withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he was speaking.

familiar.text: And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he spake.

modern.text: but they could not stand up to his wisdom or the Spirit by whom he spoke.

original.text: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυον ἀντιστῆναι τῇ σοφίᾳ καὶ τῷ πνεύματι ᾧ ἐλάλει.

verses.restored: Then they secretly stirred up men saying, We have heard him speaking blasphemous words against Moses and the Divine.

familiar.text: Then they suborned men, which said, We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses, and against God.

modern.text: Then they prompted some men to say, “We heard Stephen speak words of blasphemy against Moses and against God.”

original.text: τότε ὑπέβαλον ἄνδρας λέγοντας ὅτι Ἀκηκόαμεν αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ῥήματα βλάσφημα εἰς Μωϋσῆν καὶ τὸν θεόν·

verses.restored: They stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes; coming upon him, they seized him and brought him into the council.

familiar.text: And they stirred up the people, and the elders, and the scribes, and came upon him, and caught him, and brought him to the council,

modern.text: So they stirred up the people, elders, and scribes and confronted Stephen. They seized him and brought him before the Sanhedrin,

original.text: συνεκίνησάν τε τὸν λαὸν καὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους καὶ τοὺς γραμματεῖς, καὶ ἐπιστάντες συνήρπασαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἤγαγον εἰς τὸ συνέδριον,

verses.restored: They set up false witnesses saying, This human does not cease speaking words against this holy place and the Law.

familiar.text: And set up false witnesses, which said, This man ceaseth not to speak blasphemous words against this holy place, and the law:

modern.text: where they presented false witnesses who said, “This man never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law.

original.text: ἔστησάν τε μάρτυρας ψευδεῖς λέγοντας· Ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος οὐ παύεται ⸂λαλῶν ῥήματα⸃ κατὰ τοῦ τόπου τοῦ ⸀ἁγίου καὶ τοῦ νόμου,

verses.restored: For we have heard him say that this Jesus the Nazarene will tear down this place and change the customs Moses handed down to us.

familiar.text: For we have heard him say, that this Jesus of Nazareth shall destroy this place, and shall change the customs which Moses delivered us.

modern.text: For we have heard him say that Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs that Moses handed down to us.”

original.text: ἀκηκόαμεν γὰρ αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος οὗτος καταλύσει τὸν τόπον τοῦτον καὶ ἀλλάξει τὰ ἔθη ἃ παρέδωκεν ἡμῖν Μωϋσῆς.

verses.restored: Looking intently at him, all those sitting in the council saw his face like the face of a messenger.

familiar.text: And all that sat in the council, looking stedfastly on him, saw his face as it had been the face of an angel.

modern.text: All who were sitting in the Sanhedrin looked intently at Stephen, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.

original.text: καὶ ἀτενίσαντες εἰς αὐτὸν ⸀πάντες οἱ καθεζόμενοι ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ εἶδον τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ πρόσωπον ἀγγέλου.
